chunks: So taste (the fruit of what you sowed), for We shall add nothing but torment,

key_terms.فَذُوقُوا: So taste (imperative plural, referring to experiencing the consequence)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'So taste' imply in the context of divine punishment?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Mursalat, this verse serves as a direct response to the arrogant denial of the disbelievers, emphasizing that divine punishment is not merely a possibility but an inevitable escalation. Shia exegetes often highlight the phrase 'la nazidukum' (we will not add) to signify the completeness of their retribution, indicating that no further mercy or respite will be granted. This underscores the finality of the Hereafter for those who persist in their rejection of truth.
